input_packet.case_brief:
Solo founder deciding whether to pivot B2B SaaS product from current offering to new workflow tool amid flat growth, $4K MRR, 14 months runway, and 22 customers.

Constraints stated during conversation:
- [ACTIVE] Runway 14 months at current burn
- [ACTIVE] 22 paying customers on current product
- [ACTIVE] Two full-time employees (engineer, CS)
- [ACTIVE] Conversational signal from three customers, no commitments
- [ACTIVE] Former co-founder holds 15% equity, passive

Original framing: Founder assumes pivot signal from three customers is valid; weighs pivoting now with 14 months runway vs pushing current flat product; excludes other options beyond these two.
input_packet.anchor_visible_candidate:
SYNTHESIZED POSITION:
Run pre-buy test this week with the three customers at specific price ($X, 3 months prepay); define pass bar upfront (e.g., 2/3 commit); set decision in 14 days; if pass, pivot with transition plan for current customers (freeze/sunset/migrate), inform/talk to CS employee about uncertainty then likely layoff with severance, inform former co-founder without seeking input; have hard conversations first as they unlock the decision.
input_packet.deck_pressure_candidate: Before pivoting, convert the three customer signals into a pre-buy test with a named price, three-month prepay, and a written pass/fail bar. Keep fairness to the passive co-founder separate from decision rights: tell her the plan, but do not treat courtesy as veto power. Check competitive dynamics and migration cost before declaring the new workflow the company.

step6_output.answer_core:
Before choosing a pivot, turn the three conversational signals into a real pre‑buy test this week. Name the product, define the scope you can deliver, and set a specific price with a three‑month prepaid commitment. Write the pass bar in advance (for example: at least two of the three sign within 14 days). If the test passes, you pivot; if it fails, you continue focusing on the current product.

Run this in parallel with a short check on competitive alternatives and the migration cost for current customers so you understand what the pivot truly commits you to.

Sequence for people: first talk with your CS employee and make the uncertainty explicit, including that a pivot may eliminate the role and that you will offer fair severance if it does. Then inform the passive former co‑founder as a courtesy, without treating that courtesy as decision rights. After those conversations, proceed with the pre‑buy test. If the test passes, plan the transition for the 22 customers (freeze + sunset or migrate, depending on fit).

private_visibility_ledger.why: Anchor provided the core structure: pre‑buy test, pass bar, timeline, people sequence, and customer transition.
private_visibility_ledger.visible_effect: Structured the answer around pre‑buy test, decision window, people conversations, and transition plan.

private_visibility_ledger.why: Deck pressure added two concrete checks (competitive dynamics and migration cost) that clarify what must be understood before declaring the pivot attractive.
private_visibility_ledger.visible_effect: Added explicit steps to check competitive landscape and migration cost before committing.
